title: KV heatmap-driven memory striping for heterogeneous GPU pipelines
creator: Evan Park
description:
Problem: As tensor/pipeline parallelism increases across heterogeneous GPU clusters, KV cache microshards exhibit non-uniform access patterns. Hot microshards concentrate on a small subset of keys and frequently induce imbalanced memory pressure, cross-GPU fetches, and thermal hotspots. Existing slab/stripe allocators assume uniform access or static topology and do not account for runtime hotness or per-GPU memory pressure, causing degraded tail latency and higher network egress during streaming workloads.

Goal: Implement a heatmap-driven memory striping allocator and placement controller that continuously observes runtime key access heatmaps and per-GPU memory/thermal telemetry, and maps KV microshards to GPU memory to: (1) minimize cross-device KV transfers for hot prefixes, (2) balance memory pressure to avoid forced spills, and (3) align shard placement with tensor/pipeline parallel compute partitions to keep KV fetches local when possible.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New allocator runs in the serving runtime and produces placement decisions at runtime intervals (configurable, default 30s).
2) For steady-state streaming workload with synthetic hotkey distribution, tail P99 generation latency reduces by >=15% vs baseline striping; cross-GPU KV fetch rate reduces by >=25%.
3) GPU memory variance across nodes reduced by >=30% under heavy skew.
4) No regression in cold-start latency or correctness; evictions and spills follow defined policy and do not lose KV state.
5) Telemetry dashboards surface heatmaps and placement actions; metrics for decision rate, remap events, and migration bandwidth are available.
6) Unit and integration tests for allocator heuristics, and an e2e perf benchmark validated in staging infra.
technical_notes:
- Observability: aggregate per-prefix access counters from runtime continuous batching sampler (existing sampler hook) and merge into time-windowed heatmaps (TTL-decayed).
- Placement heuristic: cost function combining: local-hit probability (from heatmap + routing table), current GPU free memory ratio, recent spill/migration bandwidth, and per-GPU thermal pressure score.
- Granularity: operate at microshard granularity (4–16MB logical slices) to allow fine rebalancing with bounded migration cost.
- Alignment: integrate with pipeline/tensor parallel mapping to prefer co-location of microshards with partitions responsible for the same KV consumer (use placement hints from the execution planner).
- Migration: use staged async migration with write-forwarding: new writes go to both old and new locations during a short overlap window, followed by pointer flip. Uses RDMA when available, otherwise batched RPC.
- Eviction and spill: soft-evict cold microshards to host/NVMe with priority-based spill policy; hot microshards should not be spilled unless all GPUs exceed pressure threshold.
- Safety: placement controller runs in control plane with conservative rollback; every remap is idempotent and reversible.
- Config knobs: heatmap window, remap interval, microshard size, allowed migration bandwidth, thermal-safety-margin.
- Metrics: microshard_hit_rate, microshard_cross_gpu_fetches, remap_count, remap_bandwidth_bytes, per_gpu_memory_pressure, per_gpu_temperature_celsius, placement_cost_value.
implementation_steps:
1) Add heatmap aggregation to the continuous batching sampler (ENG-607002) to emit per-prefix counters and decayed windows.
2) Implement placement controller prototype as an optional runtime service in the serving process; expose gRPC control API to apply placements.
3) Implement microshard remap protocol: metadata update, staged migration, pointer flip, cleanup.
4) Integrate placement hints from the execution planner to prefer co-location with pipeline/tensor partitions.
5) Add telemetry instrumentation and dashboards for heatmaps and remap events.
6) Run microbench harness with synthetic skewed workloads; iterate heuristics.
7) Staging rollout: start with sampling-only (observer mode) -> simulated remaps -> canary remaps on non-critical tenants -> broad rollout.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: heatmap decay math, cost function edge cases, remap idempotency.
- Integration tests: end-to-end microshard migration with writes/reads during remap.
- Perf tests: compare base striping vs heatmap allocator under: Zipfian hotkeys, bursty streams, and multimodal workload mixes. Measure P50/P95/P99, cross-GPU fetches, GPU memory variance, remap bandwidth.
- Fault injection: mid-remap failures, network drop during RDMA, unexpected GPU OOM; verify rollback and safety.
- Regression: ensure no increase in cold-start latency for model loads.
- SLO gates: require P99 improvement and <5% additional background bandwidth on average for remaps.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Feature flag off (observer-only) for 2 weeks to collect heatmaps across fleet; validate heatmap quality.
Phase 1: Simulated remaps (dry-run) in dev clusters for 1 week; tune cost weights.
Phase 2: Canary on 10% of dedicated pools with non-critical tenants for 2 weeks under monitoring.
Phase 3: Expand to 50% with throttled migration bandwidth.
Phase 4: Full rollout to dedicated pools and opt-in hosted customers with opt-out.
Rollback: controller supports immediate freeze and reversal to last-good placement snapshot.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Excessive remap bandwidth can saturate interconnects and impact serving. Mitigation: enforce migration bandwidth caps, schedule remaps during lower tail windows, and allow operator-specified quiet windows.
- Risk: Heuristic oscillation where microshards ping-pong between GPUs. Mitigation: hysteresis in cost function, cooldown timers, and minimum residency.
- Risk: Inaccurate heatmaps from sampling bias. Mitigation: combine sampler with request-routing stats, expose sampling rate telemetry, and backfill with direct counters for hot prefixes.
- Risk: Thermal pressure measurement may be noisy across cloud instances. Mitigation: use smoothed temperature and leverage memory-pressure signals as primary.
- Risk: Complexity increases attack surface. Mitigation: start in opt-in mode, run extended canary, and include safety kill-switch.
